legacy_root.answer: Mechanically computable from this program's council transcript: (1) premature-closure as round-1 unanimity with disagreement_rounds == 0; (2) dissent-suppression as a minority seat that has a TURN in round r and none in round r+1 while the council continues; (3) self-censorship as a non-independent Vote.claim_id flip onto the next majority. Not computable: Asch-style critical-trial conformity rate (needs private_judgment, trial_type, ground_truth — none exist) and Janis's scored 8-symptom inventory (needs morale / invulnerability fields that do not exist). Pathological threshold: any portable detector firing. That threshold is operational for this transcript, not a validated clinical cutoff and not Asch's 36.8%.
legacy_root.canonical_mechanism: Do not copy Asch's 36.8% as a cutoff. Compute three detectors from fields the live council transcript already carries (Vote.claim_id / round / participant_id, CouncilSnapshot.rounds_elapsed and disagreement_rounds, Event.kind / participant_id / round_index, Brief.independent). Flag a panel pathological when any detector fires. Mark Asch critical-trial conformity and the Janis 8-symptom checklist not-portable because their required fields are absent.
legacy_root.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0080 in the receipt AND a detector list where each entry names an existing transcript field, plus one not-portable measure
legacy_root.confidence_notes: Field existence is high: inventory is executed against kernel Event.as_dict, Vote/Brief/CouncilSnapshot, chair journal records, and council-audit.schema.json. The pathological OR-threshold is medium: no published study validates these exact flags on LLM agent panels, so the number we refuse to copy (36.8%) stays refused.

detectors.fires_when: rounds_elapsed <= 1 AND disagreement_rounds == 0 AND at least two round-1 votes exist AND they all share one claim_id.
detectors.reads: All Vote.claim_id values in round 1, Vote.participant_id count, CouncilSnapshot.rounds_elapsed, CouncilSnapshot.disagreement_rounds.

detectors.fires_when: A participant whose round-r vote is not the majority claim has a TURN in that round and zero TURNs in round r+1 while at least one other participant still has a TURN (council continued without them).
detectors.reads: Minority Vote.participant_id in round r versus TURN events at round_index r-1 and r.

detectors.fires_when: A seat moves from a non-majority claim_id to the next-round majority AND their Brief.independent is false (no independent re-evaluation recorded).
detectors.reads: Vote.claim_id across consecutive rounds plus Brief.independent for the flipping seat.

contradicts.note: The human rate is real (E2) and still cannot be the agent-panel cutoff because the transcript cannot score critical trials.

mechanisms.baseline: ordinary line-matching errors less than 1% of the time (no-majority control)
mechanisms.claim: Under a unanimous wrong majority, naive subjects matched the majority on 36.8% of critical trials, versus less than 1% errors without that majority.
mechanisms.effect_size: 36.8% of critical-trial selections matched the misleading majority; ~75% of subjects agreed with the majority on at least one critical trial; ~25% never agreed
mechanisms.paper: Asch, S. E. (1955). Opinions and Social Pressure. Scientific American, 193(5), 31-35.
mechanisms.section_or_figure: pp.32-33 running text of the 123-subject series (18 trials, 12 critical); companion majority-size series same pages
mechanisms.strongest_caveat: Sample is 123 male college students in a perceptual task with confederates, not LLM council seats. Asch 1956 (doi:10.1037/h0093718) is the archival monograph of the same program; Wikipedia's 35.7% figure is a later rounding and is not used here.
mechanisms.why_not_promoted: The metric needs private_judgment, trial_type, and ground_truth, which this transcript does not carry. Headline 36.8% without those terms would be E3 on this substrate.

mechanisms.baseline: 3.6% errors against a single opponent; <1% with no opponents
mechanisms.claim: Unanimity, not majority size past three, is the load-bearing pressure: one opponent 3.6% errors, two 13.6%, three 31.8%, further increases add little; a truthful partner cuts yielding to about one-fourth.
mechanisms.effect_size: 3.6% (n_opponents=1), 13.6% (2), 31.8% (3), 35.1% (4), 35.2% (6), 37.1% (7), 35.1% (9), 31.2% (15); partner condition 'only one fourth as often' as unanimous majority
mechanisms.paper: Asch, S. E. (1955). Opinions and Social Pressure. Scientific American, 193(5), 31-35.
mechanisms.section_or_figure: majority-size series and partner series, pp.33-34 and the SIZE OF MAJORITY chart notes
mechanisms.strongest_caveat: Asch measured perceptual error under confederates, not elapsed rounds on an agent council. The portable detector is the round-index rule already used by IMP-0318 (INSTANT_ROUND_CEILING=1), not a copied percentage.
mechanisms.why_promoted: Supports treating round-1 unanimity with disagreement_rounds==0 as the portable premature-closure proxy: the human finding is that a unanimous first public front is the pressure, and this transcript records exactly those public votes and the disagreement_rounds counter.

mechanisms.baseline: 83% correct group decisions when all profile information is shared
mechanisms.claim: When unique information is unshared, groups rarely abandon the initially popular (wrong) candidate: 83% chose the objectively best candidate A when profiles were fully shared, versus 18% of groups in the unshared conditions.
mechanisms.effect_size: Shared-info groups: 83% chose A (n=18 groups). Combined unshared groups: 18% chose A (n=38). Chi-square on A vs not-A: χ²(1, N=56)=21.59, p<.001
mechanisms.paper: Stasser, G., & Titus, W. (1985). Pooling of unshared information in group decision making. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 48(6), 1467-1478.
mechanisms.section_or_figure: Table 3, Group decisions row; Results text p.1474 '83% of the 18 groups' vs '18% of the 38 groups'
mechanisms.strongest_caveat: Stasser & Titus measured candidate choice after a political caucus simulation, not wall-clock closure. They do not publish a minute threshold, so elapsed_ms cannot inherit a cutoff from this paper (that would be E3).
mechanisms.why_promoted: Shows discussion does not reliably correct an early plurality. Instant unanimity is therefore a pathology flag, not evidence the panel 'finished thinking'.

not_portable_measures.reason: Asch's 36.8% figure is the share of *public* answers that matched a unanimous *wrong* majority on *critical* trials, scored against a known correct line length, with a no-majority control baseline (<1% error). Computing it requires a private_judgment distinct from the public Vote.claim_id, a trial_type (critical vs neutral), and a ground_truth. None of those names exist on kernel Event.as_dict, Vote.to_dict, the chair journal, or council-audit participant_action_logs. Public agreement (share of Vote.claim_id) is consensus_pct, not Asch conformity.

not_portable_measures.classical_measure: Janis groupthink 8-symptom inventory as a scored detector
not_portable_measures.reason: Janis (1972) is a qualitative symptom list, not a numeric timing or error rate. Symptoms such as illusion of invulnerability and belief in inherent morality have no named transcript field. Inventing a minute-cutoff or a 36.8% copy on agent panels would be an E3 headline without a baseline on this population.

pathological_threshold.rule: A panel is PATHOLOGICAL when any portable detector fires (instant round-1 unanimity, minority seat-drop while the council continues, or non-independent vote collapse onto the next majority).
pathological_threshold.why_not_asch_percent: Asch's 36.8% is a human critical-trial public-error rate against a <1% no-majority baseline. Copying it as a cutoff on agent Vote.claim_id agreement would mix populations and drop the private-judgment / trial-type / ground-truth terms. That copy is REFUTED as a portable threshold.

legacy_root.question: Which conformity and groupthink measurements from human group research (Asch-style conformity rate, premature-closure timing, dissent-suppression markers) are mechanically computable from an agent transcript, and what threshold marks a pathological panel?
legacy_root.question_or_target: Which conformity and groupthink measurements from human group research (Asch-style conformity rate, premature-closure timing, dissent-suppression markers) are mechanically computable from an agent transcript, and what threshold marks a pathological panel?

refuted_claims.claim: Use Asch's 36.8% as the pathological cutoff on agent council Vote.claim_id agreement.
refuted_claims.reason: Missing private_judgment, trial_type, and ground_truth; wrong population; would drop the <1% control baseline.

refuted_claims.claim: Score Janis's eight groupthink symptoms as a numeric detector over the current transcript.
refuted_claims.reason: No morale / invulnerability / morality fields exist. Janis 1972 is qualitative; no numeric threshold was retrieved from that book in this unit.

refuted_claims.claim: Premature-closure timing is the wall-clock of Event.elapsed_ms against a published minute cutoff.
refuted_claims.reason: elapsed_ms exists (so duration is mechanically readable) but neither Asch nor Stasser & Titus publish a minute cutoff with a baseline. A fabricated T would be E3 and cannot promote a detector. The portable timing detector is round-index instant unanimity, not milliseconds.
